content.title: Combining ideas with accurate linking words
content.instructions: Combine the sentences into ONE sentence using the linker given. Keep the original meaning, change or remove words where necessary, and punctuate the linker correctly. Write the complete new sentence.

items.prompt: Online shopping is convenient. It has led to the closure of many high-street shops. Use: 'Although'
accepted_answers: Although online shopping is convenient, it has led to the closure of many high-street shops.
Online shopping has led to the closure of many high-street shops, although it is convenient.
items.model_answer: Although online shopping is convenient, it has led to the closure of many high-street shops.
items.explanation: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction that introduces the conceded (less important) idea. When the 'although' clause comes first, put a comma after it, and do not add 'but' to the main clause.

items.prompt: The price of solar panels fell dramatically. Many households installed them. Use: 'as a result'
accepted_answers: The price of solar panels fell dramatically; as a result, many households installed them.
The price of solar panels fell dramatically and, as a result, many households installed them.
The price of solar panels fell dramatically, and as a result, many households installed them.
items.model_answer: The price of solar panels fell dramatically; as a result, many households installed them.
items.explanation: 'As a result' is an adverbial linker, not a conjunction, so it cannot join two clauses with only a comma. Put a semicolon before it and a comma after it, or add the conjunction 'and'.

items.prompt: Car use in the city declined between 2005 and 2015. Cycling rates more than doubled. Use: 'whereas'
accepted_answers: Car use in the city declined between 2005 and 2015, whereas cycling rates more than doubled.
Whereas car use in the city declined between 2005 and 2015, cycling rates more than doubled.
items.model_answer: Car use in the city declined between 2005 and 2015, whereas cycling rates more than doubled.
items.explanation: 'Whereas' (like 'while') is a conjunction that contrasts two facts of equal weight, which makes it ideal for Task 1 comparisons. Put a comma before it when it comes in the middle of the sentence.

items.prompt: Millions of people still lack clean drinking water. Some governments spend billions on space exploration. Use: 'despite the fact that'
accepted_answers: Some governments spend billions on space exploration despite the fact that millions of people still lack clean drinking water.
Despite the fact that millions of people still lack clean drinking water, some governments spend billions on space exploration.
items.model_answer: Some governments spend billions on space exploration despite the fact that millions of people still lack clean drinking water.
items.explanation: 'Despite' is a preposition, so before a full clause you need 'despite the fact that'. It introduces the fact that makes the main clause surprising: the spending is surprising given the lack of clean water, so the water clause follows 'despite the fact that'.

items.prompt: Remote working reduces commuting time. It can lead to social isolation. Use: 'While'
accepted_answers: While remote working reduces commuting time, it can lead to social isolation.
While remote working reduces commuting time, it can also lead to social isolation.
items.model_answer: While remote working reduces commuting time, it can also lead to social isolation.
items.explanation: At the start of a sentence, 'While' can mean 'although', introducing a concession before the main point. The subordinate clause is followed by a comma, and the pronoun 'it' in the main clause avoids repeating 'remote working'.

items.prompt: Many schools have introduced healthy lunch menus. Childhood obesity rates remain high. Use: 'nevertheless'
accepted_answers: Many schools have introduced healthy lunch menus; nevertheless, childhood obesity rates remain high.
Many schools have introduced healthy lunch menus, but childhood obesity rates nevertheless remain high.
items.model_answer: Many schools have introduced healthy lunch menus; nevertheless, childhood obesity rates remain high.
items.explanation: 'Nevertheless' (like 'however' and 'therefore') is an adverb. To keep both ideas in one sentence, put a semicolon before it and a comma after it, or place it inside a clause introduced by 'but'.

items.prompt: The new metro line has reduced journey times. It has cut air pollution in the city centre. Use: 'In addition to' + -ing
accepted_answers: In addition to reducing journey times, the new metro line has cut air pollution in the city centre.
The new metro line has cut air pollution in the city centre in addition to reducing journey times.
items.model_answer: In addition to reducing journey times, the new metro line has cut air pollution in the city centre.
items.explanation: 'In addition to' ends in a preposition ('to'), so it takes a noun or an -ing form ('in addition to reducing'), not a base verb or a clause. The implied subject of the -ing form must be the subject of the main clause (the metro line).

items.prompt: Tuition fees rose sharply in 2012. Applications to university fell by 8%. Use: 'owing to'
accepted_answers: Applications to university fell by 8% owing to the sharp rise in tuition fees in 2012.
Owing to the sharp rise in tuition fees in 2012, applications to university fell by 8%.
Owing to a sharp rise in tuition fees in 2012, applications to university fell by 8%.
items.model_answer: Owing to the sharp rise in tuition fees in 2012, applications to university fell by 8%.
items.explanation: 'Owing to' (like 'due to' and 'because of') must be followed by a noun phrase, so the clause 'tuition fees rose sharply' becomes 'the sharp rise in tuition fees'. This nominalisation is typical of band-7+ academic writing.

items.prompt: Some countries have raised taxes on sugary drinks. They want to reduce consumption. Use: 'in order to'
accepted_answers: Some countries have raised taxes on sugary drinks in order to reduce consumption.
In order to reduce consumption, some countries have raised taxes on sugary drinks.
items.model_answer: Some countries have raised taxes on sugary drinks in order to reduce consumption.
items.explanation: 'In order to' + base verb expresses purpose when both clauses have the same subject (the countries). If the subjects were different, you would need 'so that' + clause (e.g. 'so that people drink fewer of them').

items.prompt: Cities may not invest more in public transport. In that case, traffic congestion will continue to worsen. Use: 'unless'
accepted_answers: Traffic congestion will continue to worsen unless cities invest more in public transport.
Unless cities invest more in public transport, traffic congestion will continue to worsen.
items.model_answer: Traffic congestion will continue to worsen unless cities invest more in public transport.
items.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if … not', so the negative disappears: 'unless cities invest', not 'unless cities do not invest'. Use a present tense after 'unless' even for the future, and add a comma only when the 'unless' clause comes first.
